metadata.title: Nivolumab Monotherapy – 28 day
metadata.indication: Adjuvant oesophageal or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or other appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00484 Version 13a. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: Adjuvant oesophageal or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy.
Advanced urothelial carcinoma or renal-cell carcinoma in an NCCP-listed nivolumab indication.

hypersensitivity.label: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component

pneumonitis_grade.label: Pneumonitis grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe symptoms; oxygen indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention such as ventilatory support required.

pneumonitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, oxygen requirement, imaging extent and impact on activities of daily living.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated diarrhoea/colitis grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: Neither diarrhoea nor colitis is present.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Diarrhoea: fewer than 4 stools/day above baseline or mild ostomy-output increase. Colitis: asymptomatic, clinical/diagnostic observations only.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Diarrhoea: 4-6 stools/day above baseline or moderate ostomy-output increase; limits instrumental ADL. Colitis: abdominal pain or mucus/blood in stool.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Diarrhoea: at least 7 stools/day above baseline, incontinence, hospitalisation or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care ADL. Colitis: severe abdominal pain or peritoneal signs.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening diarrhoea or colitis; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess stool increase over baseline, abdominal symptoms, bleeding, hospitalisation and peritoneal signs.

creatinine_ratio_baseline_or_uln.label: Creatinine ratio versus baseline or local ULN

alt_ast_uln_multiple.label: ALT / AST result (actual values entered; highest ×ULN calculated automatically)

bilirubin_uln_multiple.label: Bilirubin result (actual value entered; ×ULN calculated automatically)

cortisol_nmol_l.label: Cortisol (optional; interpret by sample time and steroid exposure)

myocarditis_or_neurological_red_flags.label: Possible myocarditis, myositis, encephalitis or acute neurological red flags

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion-related reaction grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade by required interruption, treatment, recurrence, hospitalisation and life-threatening features.
